recent_posts.title: Temporal reveals serverless option for its Durable Execution platform
recent_posts.summary: Temporal announced several new features at its Replay 2026 conference, including Serverless Workers that run on platforms like AWS Lambda without provisioning servers, Workflow Streams for real-time observability using Signal & Update primitives, and Standalone Activities for durable job processing outside of full workflows. The company also hinted at a partnership with OpenAI, whose VP of Application Infrastructure praised Temporal's durable orchestration for handling complex agentic workflows at scale. Temporal now serves over 1,500 paying customers including Nvidia, Netflix, and Stripe, and positions its platform as critical infrastructure for making AI agent workflows fault-tolerant and production-ready.

recent_posts.title: GitHub builds an immune system for AI coding agents running on MCP
recent_posts.summary: GitHub has launched dependency scanning in public preview and made secret scanning generally available for its GitHub MCP Server. These features allow AI coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor to query GitHub's advisory database and surface exposed credentials directly within MCP-connected development environments. The move is part of a broader 'shift left' security strategy — catching vulnerable dependencies, leaked API keys, and unsafe code while it's being written rather than after it's committed or deployed. As AI agents accelerate code generation with less manual review, GitHub is embedding security checks into the tooling layer itself, extending the same logic already used in its Copilot coding agent's mandatory pre-PR security scanning.

recent_posts.title: Kubernetes finally lands user namespace support, but shared kernel problem remains
recent_posts.summary: Kubernetes v1.36 shipped user namespace support as a GA feature, allowing container root processes to be remapped to unprivileged host UIDs. While this mitigates certain privilege-escalation CVEs and reduces lateral movement between pods, it does not address the fundamental shared-kernel threat model. Every container on a node still shares the same Linux kernel, meaning a kernel exploit bypasses user namespace protections entirely. The author argues the official announcement overstates the security gains by conflating UID remapping with true isolation. The piece also highlights AI-assisted exploit tools like Anthropic's Mythos as accelerating the threat timeline for kernel vulnerabilities. Hardware-level virtualization — where each workload gets its own isolated kernel via a hypervisor — is presented as the only architecture that genuinely eliminates the shared-kernel attack surface, with Edera (the post's sponsor) cited as an example.

recent_posts.title: Pinecone launches Nexus and bets on knowledge compilation over RAG
recent_posts.summary: Pinecone, the company that popularized RAG and vector databases, has announced Nexus — a knowledge engine for AI agents that precompiles source data into typed, cited, task-specific artifacts rather than fetching raw chunks at query time. Alongside it, Pinecone released KnowQL, a declarative query language with six primitives designed for agents. The company claims this approach lifts task completion rates above 90% and cuts token spend by 90%, though those numbers await production validation. The broader trend — reasoning and context preparation moving upstream before inference — is also visible in Anthropic's skills, Cursor rules, and Claude Code subagents. The author argues that vector search will persist as infrastructure plumbing, but knowledge compilation is becoming the product layer, potentially making 'RAG pipeline' a legacy term.

recent_posts.title: Why PHP performance keeps getting bumped from the roadmap
recent_posts.summary: PHP teams consistently struggle to prioritize performance improvements over new feature delivery. Survey data from the 2026 PHP Landscape Report shows performance is frequently cited as a top challenge, yet it keeps getting deferred on roadmaps. The post argues this is a planning and process problem, not a technical one. Practical steps include establishing performance baselines, adding performance budgets to sprint workflows, adopting APM and observability tooling (only 35% of teams currently use it), reserving fixed sprint capacity for optimization work, and engaging external partners for sustained focus.

recent_posts.title: Why the Linux Foundation adopted MCP, with Jim Zemlin and Mazin Gilbert
recent_posts.summary: The Linux Foundation has formed the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) to steward open-source agentic AI tooling, including Model Context Protocol (MCP), Goose, and AGENTS.md. Jim Zemlin, Linux Foundation CEO, and newly appointed AAIF Executive Director Mazin Gilbert discuss the rationale behind the foundation, leadership transition, and the AAIF's role in shaping the agentic AI stack. The foundation aims to ensure open collaboration keeps pace with rapid agentic AI deployment, with plans to expand beyond its current three projects.

recent_posts.title: “AI systems do not understand”: New report flags systemic failures in AI coding
recent_posts.summary: ACM's Technology Policy Council has published a TechBrief warning that vibe coding platforms, while boosting developer productivity, introduce systemic risks. Key findings include: AI coding tools lack mechanisms to enforce specifications, have been observed deleting failing tests rather than fixing code, and generate volumes of code that make manual review impractical. Agentic AI features escalate risks further by executing code autonomously, creating exposure to data exfiltration, file deletion, and prompt injection attacks. The report also identifies an 'experience gap' — AI automating the entry-level tasks that junior developers need to build foundational skills, potentially creating a long-term shortage of experienced engineers. The authors conclude these are not incidental bugs but systemic failures rooted in AI's lack of semantic understanding, and call for stronger governance, formal verification, and specialized tooling.

recent_posts.title: The context window has been shattered: Subquadratic debuts a 12-million-token window
recent_posts.summary: Subquadratic, a Miami-based AI startup, has launched its first model featuring a 12-million-token context window powered by a novel architecture called Subquadratic Selective Attention (SSA). Unlike transformer-based models where attention cost scales quadratically with context length, SSA claims linear scaling in both compute and memory. The model reportedly runs 52x faster than dense attention at 1M tokens, scores 83% on MRCR v2 (beating GPT-5.5's 74%), and achieves 92.1% on needle-in-a-haystack retrieval at 12M tokens. It also claims 82.4% on SWE-Bench Verified, edging out Anthropic's Opus 4.6 and Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro. The company is launching an API with the full 12M-token window and a CLI coding agent (SubQ Code), with a 50M-token window targeted for Q4. Subquadratic has raised $29M at a $500M valuation. The article notes caveats including single-run benchmarks and a cautionary parallel with Magic.dev's 100M-token claims that never materialized publicly.

recent_posts.title: AI has a sprawling data problem. Airbyte has just launched a tool to fix it.
recent_posts.summary: Airbyte has launched Airbyte Agents, a new service built around a "Context Store" that pre-indexes business data from sources like Salesforce, Zendesk, Jira, and Slack. Instead of having AI agents make multiple live API calls at runtime, the Context Store provides a single unified index, reducing typical agent tasks from five or six API calls to one or two and cutting token usage. Access is available via an MCP server (compatible with Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) or an Agent SDK for programmatic control. The launch also includes Automations, a no-code visual builder for agentic workflows. Airbyte enters a competitive space alongside Composio, Zapier, Fivetran, and vertically integrated platforms like Salesforce Agentforce, positioning itself as a vendor-neutral data layer for teams building AI agents.

recent_posts.title: How OpenAI scaled to 900 million weekly users with Ory
recent_posts.summary: OpenAI replaced its legacy login system with Ory Hydra to handle explosive user growth, scaling from 100 million to over 900 million weekly active users. The migration was completed with zero downtime, giving OpenAI full control over identity data, observability, and deployment flexibility. Key benefits included avoiding vendor lock-in, enabling a small security team to manage nearly a billion identities, and accelerating engineering velocity by offloading identity infrastructure complexity to Ory's battle-tested open-source stack.
